calibration.assessmentStateNote: CLOSED AT COMPUTED_VERIFIED. Arm equivalence holds: 0 divergent rows in all six scenarios (3 verticals x {compacta, amplia}, light and dark, the full 14-fixture roster), with restore exact everywhere, the negative controls held and both arms demonstrably live. It took three corrections, and none of them touched the cascade or the serving model: F4B-7 fixed the static authority door (a prose registry key that landed the stop where nothing reads it); H-3a fixed the instrument reading dependents one phase behind (27 -> 16 divergent rows); H3C delivers the DB arm write on a page that has computed nothing yet (16 -> 0). What makes the last step evidence rather than a coincidence is that the served bytes never changed: the DB arm mutateCss returns the baseline verbatim in all three phases, asserted by a drill, so a divergence that disappears cannot be attributed to a different stylesheet.

measuredResult.instrument: packages/core/src/tooling/resolution-probe, Chromium, --bundle fresh, Node 22.17.0. Both halves now: the authority door (F4B-7) and the equivalence (H3C).
measuredResult.authorityFix: ONE line. capabilities/index.ts:182 read `typography (ramp channels)`, which is prose: every walker splits on `.`, so it resolved to `typography["(ramp channels)"]` and landed the stop where nothing reads it. The real field is BrandTheme.typography.scale (themes/index.ts:568), handed to the posture lowering at brand-theme:774-791. Silent by construction, exactly like the `surfaces.density` anti-door: the seed at brand-theme:713 emits `--ds-type-scale: 1` unconditionally, so the arm never looked empty and only the stop-discrimination guard caught it. manifest ingress is derived from the registry (generator/index.mjs:246), so --sync propagated the fix and repinned the 20 registryDigests.
measuredResult.guardBeforeAfter: BEFORE: static-brand-theme THROWS "encodes NO stop" on rottay, bithire and evnto; DB PASS on all three. AFTER: static PASS with discriminating ["--ds-type-scale"] on all three; DB unchanged. 0/1 -> 1/1.
measuredResult.directChannel: Both arms, all three verticals: compacta -> 0.94 exact, amplia -> 1.06 exact. No per-vertical variation, and that is measured rather than assumed: NONE of the three verticals authors typography.scale (all three read undefined on their published baseline), so the baseline is the seed 1 everywhere.
measuredResult.identityStop: `normal` = 1 is the ramp identity and carries no receipt, like radius `suave` and density `normal`. Which of the two precedents it follows was MEASURED, not assumed: the DB arm ELIDES it (the delta is empty, so the arm emits none of the declared channels) while the static arm emits `1` because it compiles the whole theme. That is the radius shape, not the density one.

measuredResult.paintedHalf: BOTH arms move the painted ramp identically. The ramp is calc(var(--ds-font-size-*-base) * var(--ds-type-scale, 1)) at themes/default.css, and the rem root itself derives from it, so font-size, gaps and control heights all shift -- and after H3C they shift by the same amount on both doors. Supersedes the previous reading of this field, which said the DB arm moved nothing painted: that was true of the arm as it was DELIVERED then, not of the control.
measuredResult.productionUnchanged: The three compiled artifacts are byte-identical after the fix. The line corrects a door no lowering was walking; it does not change what a vertical compiles.

The DB arm models the PREVIEW path (provider-side inline emission on the document element). The productive SSR path -- server-compiled artifact embedded with visualAuthority=compiled-artifact -- is not what this arm exercises, and this row does not claim it was.

knownDefects.finding: THE INSTRUMENT READ STALE. Measured on the full 14-fixture roster through the probe own measure path: after an inline write on the document element the DEPENDENT computed properties came back ONE PHASE BEHIND -- the mutation read returned the baseline values, the removal read returned the mutation values -- while the custom property itself was always current. runtime/measure/index.mjs already documented this failure mode inside readAll; its offsetHeight flush plus a two-rAF settle was not sufficient at roster size. Evidence: packages/core/test-artifacts/quality-evidence/wo-cra-23/H3/isolation.MEASURED-NOT-RECEIPTED.json.
knownDefects.productionReading: DT ruling, and it SURVIVES the fix rather than being retired by it. The productive DB path compiles on the server and embeds the artifact for SSR, and the client hydrates that exact artifact with visualAuthority=compiled-artifact, so the served artifact carries the tenant RESOLVED values in the artifact scope itself. The probe DB arm models the PREVIEW path (provider-side emission, inline on the document element), which is the compatibility path. H3C fixed WHEN that inline write is delivered, not WHICH path is modelled: the arm is still the preview arm, and whether it should instead serve the compiled artifact remains an open fidelity decision.
knownDefects.remediation: DONE (H3C). The arm keeps its root-inline-style position -- drilled, so adopting the compiled-artifact serving path cannot slip in through this door -- and only the moment of the write changed. Serving the compiled tenant artifact stays an open FIDELITY decision about what the DB arm should model, not a cure for a symptom.
knownDefects.supersessionNote: SUPERSEDED, and the superseded entry was WRONG rather than incomplete. It claimed the vertical artifact shadowed the DB arm position because the channel is declared in the [data-ds-root] scope. Three measurements refute that: the probe scene puts data-tenant, data-ds-root and data-vertical on the SAME element (html), so there is no descendant to shadow anything; only three literal declarations of --ds-type-scale exist and all three sit at that root selector; and FOUR already-closed controls (density.mode, experience.profile, shape.radius-scale, surfaces.effect-intensity) declare their own channel in exactly that scope and closed with ingressEquivalence holding. The class does not exist. Chain of record, per AA-1: measured and written by the writer (Claude Opus) across F4B-7, the H-3 design and H-3a; adjudicated by the DT (Kimi K3), who ordered isolate-before-serve; endorsed by Fable in the H-3 preaudit (AA-1..AA-5).
knownDefects.fix: H-3a: readAll no longer trusts its first answer. It reads, provokes a full style invalidation, and reads again, accepting only after TWO consecutive identical readings, and throwing if the page never settles. Measured effect on this control, same serving model and no cascade change: light-scope divergence fell from 27 rows to 16, and card-modern-md/root now moves 15px -> 14.1px on the DB arm, byte-identical to the static arm. Invariance of the already-closed evidence was measured, not assumed: 36 stored scenarios re-run under the corrected instrument, 26212 shared movement keys compared, ZERO moved values and ZERO changed verdict legs.
knownDefects.residual: CLOSED AT ZERO, and closed by isolating it rather than by declaring it small. H3B put the same single declaration --ds-type-scale: 0.94 on one scene and one bundle through three deliveries: stylesheet-fresh (the static arm) and inline-fresh agree on every reading, while inline-live -- the DB arm as it was then -- diverged. So the residue was never the cascade, the serving model or the arm position: an inline write applied to a LIVE page leaves some elements computed against the old root, and because that state is stable it agrees with itself and the H-3a stability law cannot see it. Evidence: packages/core/test-artifacts/quality-evidence/wo-cra-23/H3/residual-isolation.MEASURED-NOT-RECEIPTED.json.
knownDefects.fixChain: THREE corrections, in order, each one measured before the next was designed. (1) F4B-7: capabilities/index.ts:182 read "typography (ramp channels)", prose that every path walker split on ".", so the static door lowered nothing -- guard 0/1 -> 1/1 on all three verticals. (2) H-3a: readAll stopped trusting its first answer (read, provoke a full style invalidation, read again, accept only after two consecutive identical readings, throw if the page never settles) -- 27 -> 16 divergent light-scope rows. (3) H3C: the DB arm delivers its write to a document that has computed nothing yet, installed before first paint and navigated per phase, exactly as the static arm already navigates -- 16 -> 0. The H-3a law is KEPT: the phase lag it catches is real and separate, and a page computed once agrees with itself immediately, so the law is now cheap rather than redundant.
knownDefects.invarianceOfPriorEvidence: Measured under the new delivery, not assumed: the 36 receipted CSS scenarios were re-run and compared BY VALUE on the intersection of movement keys -- 27076 shared keys, ZERO moved values, ZERO changed verdict legs, and zero keys present before and missing after. The new runs measure 1776 keys MORE than the stored artifacts, which is the negative-control vocabulary and the roster having grown since those rounds, not a change in what the old keys read.
knownDefects.residualSignature: WHAT THE SIXTEEN WERE, kept because a residue that vanished without its description on record is indistinguishable from one that was never measured. Two shapes, both light-scope: (a) a chain applied ONCE versus TWICE -- card-modern-md/title read 12.3375px on the DB arm (13.125 x 0.94) against 11.5972px on the static arm (13.125 x 0.94 squared), with button-modern-md/hitbox showing the same shape on height and width; (b) THREE preset-gap roots -- flex, grid and stack, across gap/column-gap/row-gap -- that the DB arm did not move at all. THREE, not four: space-modern-preset-gap was never among the probe divergences, and that absence is part of the signature rather than noise (it is the one gap that DID diverge in the isolated H3B reproduction). The four-root count in the H-3a SOURCE_READY was the writer's error and was corrected at H3B. Full row set, census and progression: packages/core/test-artifacts/quality-evidence/wo-cra-23/H3/residual-divergence.MEASURED-NOT-RECEIPTED.json.

calibration.negativeControlsScopeNote: Three, and the two that are absent are absent on purpose. "font metrics remain fixed" is what this control MOVES -- binding it would assert that the dial under test must not work. "control height remains fixed" is equally wrong here and for a measured reason rather than a cautious one: the rem root itself derives from this dial (classic/theme.css:22 sets the root font-size from --ds-font-size-base, which is calc(0.9375rem * var(--ds-type-scale, 1))), so every rem-sized control legitimately follows it -- button-modern-md/hitbox moves on both arms, in step. What remains genuinely orthogonal is colour, stroke and motion, and those three are bound at every-measured-target scope, so they are checked on all fourteen fixtures rather than on a chosen few. "border remains fixed" is deliberately NOT the entry used: it bundles the four border-*-radius longhands, which belong to shape.radius-scale, so this control would be asserting about an axis it does not own.
calibration.evidenceKindLabellingRule: One stop per proof role, so both COMPUTED_DELTA and EXACT_RESTORE are carried by real runs rather than by the same run counted twice: compacta is labelled static-db-computed-parity and amplia exact-restore. Both stops in fact prove both -- every run asserts equivalence AND exact restore -- so the labels partition the evidence, they do not narrow any run.
